messages:
Alex (eng-platform): Heads-up — received a support ticket + a customer Slack saying SLO alerts from the console are noisy and firing during normal deploys. Can we add per-route noise filtering and a default mute/snooze window in the console? cc @Maria (oncall) @Chris

Maria (eng-oncall): Yep, we see this on-call. Most noise is short spikes during deploys or retries. Per-route thresholds + a short automatic silence would help. Also need a 'dry-run' so we can validate without waking people up.

Chris (frontend): UX here matters — if we add too many knobs people will misconfigure. Can we do presets (lenient/medium/strict) and a preview that shows which routes would have triggered in the last 24h?

Vikram (eng-sre): Agree on presets. Also suggest algorithmic filtering: require sustained violation (e.g., >= 3 of 5 minutes) and detect relative jumps, not just absolute. Example rule prototype: 
```yaml
alert: route-error-spike
scope: route
window: 5m
require: samples>=3_of_5
threshold: error_rate > 3% AND relative_increase > 2x
silence_after: 30m
notify: [service-oncall, slack-channel]
dry_run: true
```
This reduces single-burst noise.

Alex (eng-platform): That `dry_run` flag is key. Also debate: default notify targets. Should console default to notifying service owners only (owner on-call) vs. fanout to org/channel? My vote: minimal default (owner only) and explicit fanout in rule. We should show expected baseline and a small sparkline next to each rule in the rule editor so users understand historical context.

Jamie (product-ops): Need telemetry to measure false positives. Add counters: total_alerts, unique_routes_alerted, alerts_silenced_by_autosilence, alerts_dry_run. We can then tune presets. Also +1 for a snooze button on the rule page and an API to programmatically mute for deploy windows.

ops-bot: [summary] 10 alerts fired in last 1h for /api/v1/embed — 7 were short spikes (~30–60s), 3 sustained. Suggested action: enable autosilence=30m + dry_run for 24h

Maria (eng-oncall): For rollout UX: can we do a canary rollout of new defaults? e.g., enable for 10% of orgs or only on newly created rules, with a console banner saying 'this rule uses new defaults (canary)'. Also allow ops to opt-in org-wide. Dry-run by default for 48h then auto-notify if no complaints.

Chris (frontend): UI sketch: slider for sensitivity with labels: Lenient (prefers silence), Balanced, Aggressive (notify quickly). Under the hood the slider maps to combos of window/requirement/relative_increase. Preview tab shows historical triggers and sample payloads.

Vikram (eng-sre): Implementation notes: we need telemetry hooks early — add reason codes to alert events (rule_evaluated, suppressed_by_autosilence, suppressed_by_require_count, dry_run_logged) so we can compute false-positive rates. Also keep rule evaluation cheap (no full-query scans).

Alex (eng-platform): Action items: 1) Vikram prototype rule evaluator changes + reason codes (Vikram) 2) Chris wireframe for presets + preview (Chris) 3) Maria coordinate dry-run with oncall team and make a list of noisy routes (Maria) 4) Jamie define telemetry metrics and dashboards (Jamie) 5) I'll add API flag `dry_run`/`autosilence` to rule model and a rollout plan. Anyone want to own the canary rollout UI copy?

Maria (eng-oncall): I can own the rollout copy + acceptance criteria for reducing noise. Proposed acceptance: 50% reduction in paging due to SLO alerts for routes on dry-run after 7 days.

Chris (frontend): I'll put up a quick mock by EOD tomorrow. Will include the preview and sensitivity slider.

Vikram (eng-sre): I'll put a small PoC in the eval service today and add the reason codes. Will post logs once ready.

Alex (eng-platform): Great — thanks. Tagging this as `p1` for the console defaults workstream. If anyone wants to add edge cases (multi-tenanted routes, quota-backed errors vs infra errors) drop them here. :thumbsup:
